title: Rapid patch orchestration and backport playflow for LTS and rolling channels
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: codify a single, developer-friendly runbook for creating emergency patches, deciding backport targets across LTS/rolling channels, and performing safe rollouts and rollbacks. This ticket unifies severity criteria, patch branch naming, automated cherry-pick tooling, CI gates, and communication templates so on-call and release engineers can move quickly and consistently.
accepted_outputs: A clear severity matrix (Sev-1..Sev-4) with time-to-action and ownership
Patch branch naming and tagging convention used by CI and release tooling
Automated pipeline job that validates cherry-picks + runs minimal acceptance matrix
Rollback playbook with automated and manual rollback steps and verification checklist
Backport decision matrix for LTS and rolling channels, including skip criteria
Communication templates for internal and customer-facing updates
Post-release verification and postmortem requirement checklist
severity_matrix: Sev-1 (Critical outage or data corruption): customer-visible production outage affecting >= 30% of traffic or any confirmed data loss/corruption. Action: 0-15m ack, 2-hour mitigation window, emergency patch branch + hot rollout. Owners: on-call SRE + release lead.

Sev-2 (Major impact): major feature degradation or extensive errors for a subset of customers (>=5% traffic) or severe performance regression. Action: 15-60m ack, 24-hour remediation target. Owners: on-call + assigned eng on call.
Sev-3 (Medium): functionality degraded for small subset, or non-critical incorrect behavior. Action: triage within 24h, targeted patch in next patch cycle. Owners: product/engineer owner.
Sev-4 (Low): minor bugs, docs, or non-blocking regressions. Action: backlog; plan in next sprint. Owners: product/feature team.
patch_branching: Base branch selection: create patch branch from the exact Git tag used for release (git checkout -b from v1.24.2). Do not branch from main unless release tag missing and authorized by release lead.
Small diffs only: patches must be limited to the minimum change set required to resolve the severity; include unit + smoke tests only. No refactors or unrelated changes.
Tagging: final patch commit must be tagged v<major>.<minor>.<patch>+hotfix.<n> when appropriate and pushed to protected release refs.
PR process: use the emergency PR template that includes impact assessment, backport targets, and verification steps. Require two approvals: release lead + security if security_review_required = true.
backport_policy: Always backport: security fixes (CVE-like), data corruption fixes, and crashers causing broad availability impact (Sev-1/2).
Conditional backport: user-facing regressions and performance critical fixes — use the backport decision matrix below to choose targets.
Skip backport when: fix depends on a refactor or newmajor infra change; risk of destabilizing LTS is high and customers on that channel are unaffected.

Targets: For each fix, enumerate targets from highest to lowest priority: current rolling (main), current minor stable (e.g., 1.24.x), active LTS channels (e.g., LTS-2025), and legacy LTS only if customers explicitly requested and signed off by CSM.

Backport rules: 1) Reproduce on target branch. 2) Cherry-pick commit(s) into target branch. 3) Run the minimal acceptance matrix (smoke + targeted e2e). 4) Label backport PR with backport/<target> and link original ENG key.
automated_checks_and_ci: New pipeline job: release/pch-validate which: checks cherry-pick cleanliness, runs unit tests, executes smoke acceptance suite, and verifies dependency locks. Fails fast if conflicts need manual resolution.

Canary verification job: runs telemetry validation against a short-lived canary cluster (5-10% traffic) and computes rolling metrics: error_rate, p95_latency, request_drop. Gate threshold defaults: error_rate > 0.5% OR p95_latency regress > 20% => block rollout.
Auto-tagging: on merge to release/<x.y.z>-patch/* branches, CI creates a release candidate artifact and publishes metadata to the release registry (artifact + changelog + ENG key).
Automated rollback trigger: if canary job notices threshold breach, CI triggers automated rollback to previous tag and opens ENG revert PR with logs and metric diffs.
Security checks: static analysis and dependency scan must pass for any patch that touches service boundaries; otherwise security approval required prior to merge.
rollout_gates_and_verification: Canary phase: 0-10% small cohort for 30-60 minutes; verify telemetry and any customer-facing metrics.
Staged ramp: 10->50% over configurable windows (default: 60m per step) if canary stable. Monitor SLO windows for regressions.
Full rollout: after 2 successful staging windows (low error rate and stable latency), proceed to 100% rollout with standard release notes and changelog.
Rollback criteria: immediate rollback if persistent error_rate above threshold for >10 minutes, or sustained p95 latency regress >20% for >15 minutes, or evidence of data corruption.
rollback_playbook: Immediate steps: 1) Declare incident and set severity. 2) Stop the rollout or trigger CI rollback job. 3) If automated rollback fails, manual rollback: kubectl rollback / deploy previous image tag or flip traffic in routing layer.
Verification: after rollback, confirm 5 golden transactions and key user flows succeed; check metrics for at least 30 minutes in production and canary histograms return to baseline.
Communication: post internal incident update within 30 minutes summarizing cause, action taken, customer impact and mitigation plan. External customer advisory within 2 hours if customers impacted.
Follow-up: open a postmortem task; require root-cause analysis and a remediation plan with owner and due date within 5 working days.
communication_templates: Internal incident update (short): [ENG-45219] Sev-1 rollback executed for runtime-1.24.2+hotfix. Action: rolled back to v1.24.1. Impact: 22% of requests affected. Next: postmortem assigned to @LiamChen.

Customer advisory (external): We identified a production regression affecting text generation latency for a subset of requests. We rolled back the change and full service is restored. A postmortem and timeline will be shared within 72 hours. Contact support@redwood.ai for questions.
PR template snippet: include sections - Summary, Severity, Root-cause hypothesis, Affected releases (list tags), Backport targets recommended, Verification steps run, Rollout plan and gates.
audit_and_postmortem_requirements: Every Sev-1/2 patch requires a postmortem published to Confluence within 72 hours and a 1:1 blameless review with stakeholders.
All emergency patches must reference the PR/commit in the release register and include the list of cherry-picks applied to each target branch.
For LTS releases, maintain an audit CSV with: release tag, patch tag, ENG key, PR link, testing matrix results, and customer notifications.
examples_and_runbook_links: Example: ENG-39721 resolved a Sev-1 cache corruption via release/1.22.4-patch/ENG-39721 - reproducible steps and cherry-picks are linked in the PR.
notes: Decision: when in doubt for LTS backports, default to preserve customer stability; require CSM signoff to add legacy backport targets.
Trade-off: smaller hotfixes reduce risk but increase number of backports; larger combined fixes are riskier to merge into stable channels.
Follow-ups: implement automated cherry-pick assistant in cycle 2026-Q2 to reduce manual conflict resolution time.
